cues.zh: 我爱 Ruby。

cues.zh: 我们不是都爱 Ruby 吗？它很棒。

cues.en: by seeing how much Ruby can do if we remove all of its features.
cues.zh: 看看如果把它的特性全删掉，Ruby 还能干多少事。

cues.en: So by that I mean, let's not use any gems. Let's not use the standard library. Let's not make use of any modules, any classes, no objects, no methods. Also, no control flow, no assignment, arrays, strings, numbers, or booleans.
cues.zh: 我的意思是：不用任何 gem，不用标准库，不用任何模块、任何类，没有对象，没有方法。还有，不要控制流、不要赋值、不要数组、字符串、数字，也不要布尔值。

cues.en: Just before I continue, I've just gotta say to you that this is just a game. It is not software engineering advice. So
cues.zh: 在继续之前，我得先说明：这只是一个游戏，不是软件工程建议。所以

cues.en: here are the rules of the game that we're going to play.
cues.zh: 下面就是我们要玩的这个游戏的规则。

cues.en: We're gonna be allowed to create prox and call prox.
cues.zh: 我们允许创建 Proc 和调用 Proc。

cues.en: Also, for sort of practical purposes, I'm gonna allow us to abbreviate bits of code with constants. So what I mean is if I'm gonna make a big long prox, I'm gonna assign that to a constant, give it a name, then use it again later. But that's really just the same as using that big string of code again. This will just help make it a bit more readable and importantly, it's not lending any kind of utility to the code that I'm gonna write.
cues.zh: 另外，出于实用考虑，我允许我们用常量来缩写一些代码片段。我的意思是，如果我要写一个很长的 proc，我会把它赋值给一个常量，给它起个名字，然后再在后面使用它。但这实际上就跟再次使用那一长串代码是一样的。这只是为了让代码更易读一点，重要的是，它并不会给我将要写的代码带来任何额外的功能。

cues.en: So, the goal of this game is going to be to write the FizzBuzz
cues.zh: 那么这个游戏的目标就是写出 FizzBuzz

cues.en: program, which you probably all know about. But this is something that you can ask someone in a programming interview
cues.zh: 程序，你们可能都知道这个。但这是你在编程面试中可以问别人的一个问题

cues.en: just to check to see whether they are lying about being a programmer.
cues.zh: 就是为了检验他们是不是在谎称自己是程序员。

cues.en: Because it's it's ostensibly very simple. You write a program that prints the numbers from one to a 100. For multiples of three, you print fizz instead of the number. For multiples of five, you print buzz instead of the number. And for multiples that are both, for numbers which are multiples of both three and five, print fizz buzz. So, this is very straightforward and hopefully everyone in this room just knows how to do that.
cues.zh: 因为它表面上非常简单。你写一个程序，打印从 1 到 100 的数字。对于 3 的倍数，你打印 fizz 而不是数字。对于 5 的倍数，你打印 buzz 而不是数字。而对于同时是 3 和 5 的倍数的数字，打印 fizz buzz。所以，这非常直截了当，希望这个房间里的每个人都知道怎么做。

cues.en: So, given that I'm gonna be using procs, let me just talk about procs for a second.
cues.zh: 那么，既然我要用到 proc，让我先简单说说 proc。

cues.en: The thing about procs is that they're really just plumbing in your program. They don't really do very much apart from move values around. So, if you've got a proc like this, then what happens when you call, when you do this call here, is that the value that you've passed in, in this case 41, just kind of flows into the the parameter, to the block that you've, that you've given. And then of course, that value kind of flows to all the places where that parameter is used. And then effectively what Ruby ends up evaluating is this kind of 41 plus one. So, it's the rest of the language, the rest of Ruby that does the actual work. The props are really just kind of wiring bits of the program together.
cues.zh: proc 的特点在于，它们其实只是程序里的管道。除了传递值之外，它们并不真正做太多事情。所以，如果你有这样一个 proc，那么当你调用、当你在这里执行这个调用时，你传入的值，在这个例子中是 41，就会流入你给出的那个块的参数中。然后当然，那个值会流向所有使用该参数的地方。然后实际上 Ruby 最终求值的就是这种 41 加 1。所以，是语言的其余部分、Ruby 的其余部分在做实际的工作。proc 其实只是把程序的各个部分连接在一起。

cues.en: Another thing to point out that some of you will know is that prox don't actually need to have multiple arguments, technically.
cues.zh: 另一点需要指出的是——你们有些人可能已经知道——严格来说，proc 其实并不需要接受多个参数。

cues.en: If you've got a prox like this in Ruby that takes two arguments and then you pass in two arguments. You can just as well write that with a kind of two nested prox. You've probably seen this before.
cues.zh: 如果你在 Ruby 里有一个像这样接受两个参数的 proc，然后传入两个参数，你也完全可以用两个嵌套的 proc 来实现同样的效果。你以前可能见过这种写法。

cues.en: There's a proc here that takes the first argument and it returns another proc that takes the second argument, I can just call the first proc with x and then call the second proc with y. And it's exactly the same. This is called currying incidentally and you can call curry on a proc object to do this transformation.
cues.zh: 这里有一个 proc 接收第一个参数，然后返回另一个接收第二个参数的 proc。我可以先用 x 调用第一个 proc，再用 y 调用第二个 proc，效果完全一样。顺便说一下，这叫做柯里化（currying），你可以在 proc 对象上调用 curry 来完成这种转换。

cues.en: Another point to make, slightly more esoteric, is that procs are kind of,
cues.zh: 还有一点要讲，稍微更玄一点，那就是 proc 某种程度上……

cues.en: they're opaque really. The only way that you can see inside them or do anything with them is just to call them. And one consequence of this, which is gonna seem a little bit
cues.zh: 它们其实是不透明的。要看清它们内部、或者对它们做任何操作的唯一方式，就是调用它们。由此带来的一个结果——现在提起来可能有点

cues.en: little bit random to mention now, but will be useful later. Is that if you've got a proc like this, which all it does is take an argument and then call some other proc with that argument. That's the same as just using the prop that's inside. These two things do the same job.
cues.zh: 有点没头没脑，但后面会派上用场。那就是：如果你有一个这样的 proc，它唯一做的事就是接收一个参数，然后用这个参数去调用另一个 proc，这和直接使用里面那个 proc 是等价的。这两个东西干的是同样的活。

cues.en: This outermost proc here just passes the argument on through to the one inside. So, the reason I'm mentioning it now is because this is kind of a refactoring opportunity
cues.zh: 最外层的这个 proc 只是把参数原封不动地传给里面那个。我现在提这个的原因是，这其实算是一个重构的机会

cues.en: and you might be able to, if you see this in your program, you might be able to turn it into that. And for some reason, you might wanna turn this back into that as well.
cues.zh: 如果你在自己的程序里看到这种写法，也许可以把它简化成那种形式。而出于某些原因，你可能也想把它再变回那种嵌套的形式。

cues.en: So, just before I begin properly, I just wanna make a little syntactic point.
cues.zh: 那么，在正式开始之前，我想先讲一点语法上的小问题。

cues.en: I'm sure you all know that in Ruby, there are several ways to create a proc. You can use proc dot new or you can use kernel dot proc or you can use kernel dot lambda. And in Ruby 1.9, you can use this kind of swanky, stabby lambda syntax.
cues.zh: 我相信你们都知道，在 Ruby 里有好几种创建 proc 的方式。可以用 proc.new，可以用 Kernel.proc，也可以用 Kernel.lambda。而在 Ruby 1.9 里，还可以用这种很花哨的短箭头 lambda 语法。

cues.en: Similarly, if you want to call a proc,
cues.zh: 同样，如果你想调用一个 proc，

cues.en: you can use the call method. You can use square brackets. You can use triple equals in Ruby 1.9 in case you wanna put your proc in a case statement.
cues.zh: 可以用 call 方法。可以用方括号。在 Ruby 1.9 里还可以用 ===，方便把 proc 放进 case 语句里。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: and you can also use round brackets in Ruby 1.9. Now, just for the purposes of like, basically,
cues.zh: 在 Ruby 1.9 里还可以用圆括号。现在，基本上只是为了说明，

cues.en: these are all equivalent roughly. I mean, you'll know that prox and lambdas are not quite the same thing, but for the purpose of this talk, I'm just gonna ignore that.
cues.zh: 这些大致都是等价的。我的意思是，你们知道 proc 和 lambda 并不完全相同，但为了这次演讲，我先忽略这一点。

cues.en: And, I'm just gonna choose a syntax. In fact, instead of doing this lambda blah de blah dot call, I'm just gonna say stabby and square brackets. Mostly because this just kind of reduces the syntactic noise and lets you concentrate on what's actually happening. I'm not, this isn't necessarily the best syntax for lambdas. It's just the most convenient for what I'm gonna show you today. Okay, go.
cues.zh: 而且，我就选一种语法。其实，与其写这种 lambda 这堆那堆再 .call，我干脆用短箭头加方括号。主要是因为这样能减少语法噪音，让你专注于实际发生的事情。我不是说，这不一定是 lambda 的最佳语法，只是对我今天要展示的内容最方便。好，开始。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: first of all, first
cues.zh: 首先，首先

cues.en: of all, here is FizzBuzz written in Ruby. I am available for freelance programming.
cues.zh: 首先，这是用 Ruby 写的 FizzBuzz。我目前可以接自由职业编程项目。

cues.en: Again, this is not necessarily the best implementation of FizzBuzz or the cleverest. You've probably seen some very clever implementations on the internet. This is just like, when I sit down to just write it straight out, this is what I would write without thinking about it. So I'll say right off the bat that I'm not even gonna try and implement this because it does a bunch of, it's got some puts statements in it which involve printing text onto the console and I can't print text onto the console if I'm only using procs. So, what I'm gonna do is replace it with a roughly equivalent program which is just mapping over this array of numbers from one to a 100 and just, so what you're gonna get out of this is an array of strings rather than putting them to the console. But hopefully, you will agree that that is not too much of a fudge.
cues.zh: 再说一次，这不一定是 FizzBuzz 最好或最聪明的实现。你们可能在网上见过一些非常聪明的实现。这更像是，当我坐下来直接写出来时，不假思索就会写成这样。所以我先说明，我根本不打算实现它，因为它里面有一些 puts 语句，涉及把文本打印到控制台，而如果我只用 proc，就没法把文本打印到控制台。所以我要做的是，把它换成一个大致等价的程序：只是对 1 到 100 的数字数组做 map，这样你得到的是一个字符串数组，而不是把它们输出到控制台。但希望你们会同意，这不算太敷衍。

cues.en: Before I continue, I'll say that this is,
cues.zh: 在我继续之前，我想说，这，

cues.en: somewhat surprising. This is quite an ambitious program, really. If you don't have any of the features of a programming language. Because we're doing, we create a range and then we map over it. And then we do a bunch of arithmetic using the modulus operator.
cues.zh: 有点让人意外。这确实是一个相当宏大的方案。如果你完全不具备编程语言的任何特性。因为我们在做的是，我们创建一个范围，然后对它进行映射。接着我们使用取模运算符做一堆算术运算。

cues.en: We use zero predicate on those numbers that we're creating. We've got some strings and we've got number to string here. And we've also got a big condition around the outside of it. So there's quite a lot of functionality there that we're just using. So I'm gonna have to go through and kind of implement all of this stuff without using any of it. Just using prox. So first of all, what I'm gonna focus my attention on is just these, all of the numbers that appear in this code and see how we can represent those and implement them without actually using Ruby's numbers.
cues.zh: 我们在创建的这些数字上使用零谓词。这里有一些字符串，还有数字转字符串的操作。在它的外围还有一个大大的条件判断。所以这里有很多我们正在使用的功能。因此我得逐个走查，并在不使用这些特性的情况下把它们全实现出来。只使用 proc。所以首先，我关注的重点是，这段代码中出现的所有数字，看看如何在不实际使用 Ruby 数字的情况下表示和实现它们。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: how can you possibly represent numbers
cues.zh: 你到底怎么去表示数字呢？

cues.en: without using any, any data? You know, any of the data types that Ruby provides you with and only using code.
cues.zh: 在不使用任何、任何数据的情况下？你知道的，就是不使用 Ruby 提供给你的任何数据类型，只使用代码。

cues.en: All the code that we, we're writing can do is make a proc or call a proc.
cues.zh: 我们编写的所有代码能做的，就是创建一个 proc 或调用一个 proc。

cues.en: And pretty much the, the simplest way, although there are several different ways of doing it. The simplest way to represent numbers in this way is just to represent a number n with some code that calls some other proc n times. So, what I mean by that is, if I was allowed to define methods, which I'm not. But if I was, what I would do is say, I'm gonna make the number one and that's gonna be a method that takes some other proc as it's first argument and then some arbitrary second argument and it just calls the proc with that argument once.
cues.zh: 差不多最简单的方法——尽管有几种不同的实现方式。用这种方式表示数字最简单的方法，就是用一段会调用其他 proc n 次的代码来表示数字 n。所以，我的意思是，如果我被允许定义方法，虽然我不行。但如果可以的话，我会说，我要创造数字 1，它是一个方法，接受另一个 proc 作为它的第一个参数，然后是一个任意的第二个参数，它只是用那个参数调用该 proc 一次。

cues.en: And then I could define two, which calls proc with that argument once, and then calls the proc again, with whatever the result of calling it the first time was, and so on. I can keep going for ages like this.
cues.zh: 然后我可以定义 two，它先用那个参数调用一次 proc，再用第一次调用的结果再次调用该 proc，依此类推。我可以一直这样写下去。

cues.en: Also, there's a fairly obvious,
cues.zh: 另外，还有一个挺显而易见的……

cues.en: If you extrapolate backwards, there's a fairly obvious way of implementing zero, which is just to say zero is the is the method that takes a proc and an argument and doesn't call the proc at all. It just returns whatever the second argument was.
cues.zh: 如果反向推导，实现 zero 的方式其实很显而易见：zero 就是一个接受一个 proc 和一个参数的方法，并且完全不调用这个 proc，只是直接返回第二个参数。

cues.en: So all of these I can translate into a kind of a method less representation by just saying, well, I could represent this method one here as a proc that takes two arguments and then calls the first argument with the second one. And so, it would look like this. So that's just kind of taking away the method definition stuff like I said I wasn't allowed to use. And instead, I'm just gonna define each of these. Zero is a proc that takes some other proc and some value and just returns the second value and so on.
cues.zh: 所以所有这些我都可以转换成一种“无方法”的表示形式，比如，我可以把这里的 one 方法表示成一个接受两个参数的 proc，然后用第二个参数去调用第一个参数。它看起来就会像这样。这就去掉了我之前说过不能使用的方法定义语法。取而代之的是，我直接这样定义它们每一个：zero 是一个接受另一个 proc 和某个值的 proc，并且直接返回第二个值，依此类推。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: the main problem with programming like this is that if I were to type any of these on the console to Ruby and inspect it, it would just say, well, what you've got there is a proc. So I can't really make use of these without some kind of way of,
cues.zh: 这样编程的主要问题在于，如果我在 Ruby 控制台里输入其中任何一个并 inspect 它，它只会显示“你拿到的是一个 proc”。所以如果不借助某种方式，我根本没法真正使用它们……

cues.en: you know, if I wanted to write some tests for example. I would probably want my tests to be able to test against Ruby values, not these kind of mental ones that I've, that I've implemented with procs. So, what you can do is implement, say in your test helpers or in some kind of external library that is interfacing
cues.zh: 比如，如果我想写一些测试。我大概会希望测试针对的是真实的 Ruby 值，而不是我用 proc 实现的这些反人类的玩意儿。所以你能做的，就是在比如测试辅助函数或某个外部库里实现对接，

cues.en: with this mad code that you're writing. You could write something like this for example. So you could say, well I'm gonna have a method called two integer which is gonna take one of these procs that represents a number. And what I'm gonna do with that prox that represents a number is pass it another prox that just increments it's argument. And then the thing that I'm gonna ask it to apply that to however many times is is zero. So, if I plug in
cues.zh: 来对接你写的这些疯狂代码。比如你可以写成这样：定义一个叫 to_integer 的方法，它接收一个代表数字的 proc。然后我给这个代表数字的 proc 传入另一个只负责让参数自增的 proc。而我让它重复应用该操作的初始值是 0。所以，如果我传入……

cues.en: if I plug in zero into this, then I get a real Ruby zero back. And if I plug in three, I get a real Ruby three back.
cues.zh: 如果我把 zero 传进去，就能拿回一个真正的 Ruby 0。如果传进 three，就能拿回一个真正的 Ruby 3。

cues.en: So, I can also implement, I mean, for my fizz buzz I needed five and fifteen and a 100. So, I can implement those as well.
cues.zh: 所以，我也可以实现，我是说，我的 FizzBuzz 需要 5、15 和 100。所以这些我也能实现。

cues.en: These aren't very compact definitions of those numbers, but these will work. And if I plug those into my kind of two integer method, will get back the real, you know, Ruby five, fifteen and hundred.
cues.zh: 这些数字的定义不算很紧凑，但能用。如果把它们代入我那个接收两个整数的方法，就能拿回真正的 Ruby 的 5、15 和 100。

cues.en: So going back to my fizz buzz, all of those numbers I can just replace them, And you know, rather than inlining that whole massive term there, I'm just gonna put the constants in so you can see that I've replaced them. So that's great. I've got rid of the numbers. Of course the problem with this is that that code doesn't work anymore because I was calling operations like modulus and stuff on those numbers. And because Ruby doesn't know what they are, it doesn't do anything. So I need to go and replace all of the other operations in that code before it'll work.
cues.zh: 那么回到我的 FizzBuzz，所有这些数字我都可以直接替换掉。你知道，与其把那一大串内联进去，我干脆把常量放进去，这样你能看到我已经替换了它们。这很好，我把数字去掉了。当然，问题是这样代码就不能再工作了，因为我之前是在这些数字上调用取模之类的操作。而 Ruby 不知道它们是什么，所以什么也不做。因此我需要把代码里所有其他操作也替换掉，它才能工作。

cues.en: So moving on to how I'm gonna deal with the boolean stuff. How
cues.zh: 接下来讲我怎么处理布尔值这部分。怎么

cues.en: can I represent booleans without any data? Like using only code and only procs.
cues.zh: 我才能在没有数据的情况下表示布尔值？比如只用代码、只用 proc。

cues.en: Well, the thing about booleans is is that they are used for choosing, you know, between two options. When you've got a conditional, you will say, you know, either if some boolean then this block else that block, in which case the boolean is just allowing you to pick one or the other. Or in Ruby, more often than not, what you're doing is saying, if some boolean, then do this and then in your mind you're thinking, else nil.
cues.zh: 布尔值的关键在于，它们用来在两个选项之间做选择，你知道。当你有一个条件语句时，你会说，如果某个布尔值成立就执行这个块，否则执行那个块；这种情况下，布尔值只是让你二选一。或者在 Ruby 里，更常见的是，你说如果某个布尔值成立就做这个，然后心里想着，否则就是 nil。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: what you, the, you can take advantage of this by representing a boolean with some code that is gonna choose one of two values. So we can kind of cut out the middle man and say, we don't need some data that we're gonna use to later decide which of those blocks we can choose. We can just implement booleans as either something that chooses the first thing or something that chooses the second thing. So if I was gonna write these, oops, sorry, as methods, I could just say, well true is this method that takes two arguments and returns the first one. And false is a method that takes two arguments and returns the second. So again, writing these as prox like that, you can see that that's a pretty straightforward translation.
